newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Tosovsky foresees little pressure on Czech crown.
newsitem.headline: Tosovsky foresees little pressure on Czech crown.

text.p: Czech National Bank Governor Josef Tosovsky on Wednesday said he foresees little pressure on the exchange rate of the crown in the near future.
In a speech to a business forum in Prague he said devaluation of the crown would not solve current export problems, which have helped cause a record trade gap over the first nine months of the year.
"Pressure for a change to the exchange rate is not threatening in the present, and also not in the near future," Tosovsky said.
"Devaluation is always an inflationary factor and we want the exact opposite. Devaluation promotes exports with low added value and we want the exact opposite," he said.
Tosovsky said a devaluation would also create demand for increased wages due to the higher cost of imports, especially of consumer goods.
"With a policy of a soft currency we could get into an inflation-devaluation spiral," he said.
He said the central bank instead will continue to push for lowering inflation and a stable exchange rate which should, in the longer-term, help exports.
